fixed_shape.exact_solution: q=q0>0, p=0, N(t)>0 arbitrary; auxiliary torsion zero
fixed_shape.integrable_variations: u=a; b=0 follows from second-order real lapse constraint
fixed_shape.endpoint_conditions: Dirichlet q at both ends; gauge xi(t_i)=xi(t_f)=0
fixed_shape.boundary_data: A solution exists only when prescribed endpoint q values agree. With fixed values q0 is fixed; q0 varies across boundary data.
fixed_shape.lapse_modulus: For endpoint-preserving reparametrizations, T=integral N dt is invariant. At fixed T every zero-integral lapse variation is gauge; if T is not fixed it remains a global interval parameter.
fixed_shape.presymplectic: Pullback of dq wedge dp plus dN wedge dp_N to exact solutions is zero. Its kernel includes q0 and, if varied, T, which are not generated by endpoint-preserving time reparametrization.
fixed_shape.scope: Common-scale finite-dimensional truncation only; no full gravity spectrum or dynamical instability claim

point_coordinates.conclusion: The zero-gradient quadratic constraint persists under a smooth invertible canonical point transformation.

endpoints.fixed_boundary_statement: If q at both endpoints is held at the same q0, u_i=u_f=0 already forces a=b=0 in the linear ODE. The spurious b mode is a feature of the local/initial-value linearized equation or of varying boundary data, not a surviving fixed-two-endpoint Dirichlet fluctuation.
endpoints.variable_boundary_statement: Across exact solutions the two q boundary values must vary together. Their common variation a changes spatial volume and is not time gauge.
endpoints.interval_statement: Endpoint-preserving time diffeomorphisms fix T=integral N dt; lapse profiles with the same T are gauge-related. If T is allowed to vary it is a separate interval parameter.

mixed_shape.exact_metric: q0^2 exp(epsilon M0) (1+3 epsilon h tau)^(2P) exp(epsilon M0), M0=a I+B0; positive interval
mixed_shape.exact_scale: q0 exp(epsilon a) (1+3 epsilon h tau)^(1/3)
mixed_shape.integrability: All real homogeneous linearized directions on the cone integrate locally: h!=0 uses the exact family; h=0 forces Sigma=0 and leaves static metric moduli.
mixed_shape.endpoints: Local/initial-data or varying-boundary comparison. Holding both metric endpoints fixed at the background removes the affine first-order coefficients.
mixed_shape.scope: Finite homogeneous sector on a fixed torus; no full gravitational degree count or global-in-time stability claim.

figure_slice.description: Two orthonormal shear directions; a three-dimensional slice of the five-shear constraint cone.
